bugs.error_message: RAY_STR sort quadratic on long common prefixes
bugs.root_cause: strsort_aflag fell through to insertion_sort when bp >= parts_bytes (packed window exhausted with a big bucket still to sort). Insertion sort is O(n^2), catastrophic on inputs where many strings share a prefix longer than parts*8 bytes.
bugs.fix: Added strsort_repack_window: when current window is exhausted on a bucket larger than the base-case threshold, re-materialize the next parts*8 bytes of each record's original string as new parts[], reset bp=0, continue the radix. Threaded base_offset through strsort_aflag to track consumed bytes. Keeps worst case at O(total string bytes).

bugs.error_message: RAY_STR run-detection shortcut false-positive on all-equal packed keys
bugs.root_cause: strsort_detect_runs declared the non-null range already-sorted whenever adjacent packed keys were all equal. For inputs sharing a prefix longer than parts*8 bytes, all packed keys tie but real tail-byte ordering remained unresolved — the shortcut returned unsorted data.
bugs.fix: On a packed-key tie, check whether either string has len > parts_bytes. If so, tail bytes may impose ordering we haven't seen — return 0 and fall through to the full sort rather than declaring a run. Added /lang/sort/long_common_prefix regression test.

bugs.error_message: RAY_STR sort hist/off OOM fallback double-frees tmp scratch
bugs.root_cause: The parallel top-level partition's hist/off OOM branch freed tmp_hdr before falling through to sequential strsort_aflag. The outer cleanup block (`if (tmp_hdr) scratch_free(tmp_hdr)`) then freed the same header a second time — scratch_free is NULL-safe but does NOT protect against freeing an already-freed non-NULL header.
bugs.fix: Dropped the inner scratch_free(tmp_hdr) from the OOM branch. tmp_hdr now belongs exclusively to the outer cleanup block, which frees it exactly once regardless of whether the parallel path completed normally or fell back to sequential.

bugs.error_message: RAY_STR sort loses correctness for embedded 0x00 bytes / prefix-of-each-other strings
bugs.root_cause: strsort_repack_window short-circuited with any_tail=false whenever every string in a bucket ended at or before the current base_offset — but within such a bucket records can still have different lengths (e.g. 'abc' and 'abc\0\0' tie bit-for-bit on the zero-padded packed prefix). ray_str_t_cmp puts the shorter prefix first, but the caller just returned without ordering by len, leaving buckets > the insertion-sort base case in arbitrary order. Visible on inputs with embedded NUL bytes or strict-prefix string pairs.
bugs.fix: Track min/max string length while repacking. When any_tail is false AND min_len != max_len AND n > 1, call a new strkey_qsort_by_len (in-place median-of-3 quicksort with insertion-sort base case, single-key integer sort on the len field) to finalize the bucket in O(n log n). When min_len == max_len every record is bitwise identical so the sort is skipped, preserving few_unique performance. Added /lang/sort/embedded_nul regression test covering 50 'abc\0\0' interleaved with 50 'abc' — verified failing without the fix and passing with it.

Also handle the legacy bare-column form {name: Col} to preserve existing map-group test behavior (null placeholder column).
